product_name: boAt Bassheads 100 in-Ear Wired Earphones with Mic (Black)
reviews: [★5] Cheap backup earphones - For under 400 rupees the bass is decent enough for casual podcast listening while commuting.
[★5] Funky hawk inspired design - The angular earbud shell looks unique and fits snugly into the ear canal without slipping.
[★5] Good inline mic for calling - Works fine for quick phone calls and hands-free voice notes.
[★5] Value for pocket money - Decent budget option for college students who keep misplacing expensive wireless earbuds.
[★4] Okay sound for the price - Heavy bass response though vocals sound slightly muffled compared to premium earphones.
[★4] Decent build for 350 Rs - Tangle-free cable coating helps prevent messy knots inside pocket.
[★4] Fits comfortably with small ear tips - Includes three sizes of silicone ear tips that seal ambient room noise moderately.
[★4] Loud output volume - 10mm dynamic drivers produce high sound pressure without requiring high volume on phone.
[★3] Muddy soundstage - Overpowering artificial bass drowns out midrange instruments and subtle acoustic details.
[★3] Plastic feels cheap and hollow - Shell is made of lightweight brittle plastic that scratches easily.
[★3] Mic button is stiff - Single inline button requires hard press to pause tracks or answer incoming phone calls.
[★3] Microphonics noise from cable - Any rubbing of the wire against your shirt transmits annoying rustling sounds directly to your ears.
[★3] Average durability - Survived daily train commute for 2 months before audio balance started fluctuating.
[★2] One side stopped working within 3 weeks - Left earbud went completely dead without any physical drops or water exposure. Extremely fragile internal wiring.
[★2] Thin flimsy cable near jack - Wire near the 3.5mm connector has zero strain relief and snapped after normal pocket bending.
[★2] Ear pain after 30 minutes - Hard plastic edges of the hawk contour press uncomfortably against the ear concha causing soreness.
[★2] Terrible harsh treble at high volumes - Cymbals and sharp s sounds pierce your eardrums with painful tinny distortion above 60% volume.
[★2] Cheap rubber ear tips tear easily - Silicone tips ripped in half while changing them to test a different size fit.
[★2] Disappointing microphone clarity - Callers frequently complain that my voice sounds distant, hollow, and muffled during calls.
[★2] Fails after mild moisture - Sweat from morning jog caused crackling audio distortion in the right driver.
[★2] High failure rate - Replaced under warranty once and the replacement unit failed within 25 days with the exact same dead left earbud.
[★1] Absolute waste of money - Stopped functioning after barely 12 days. Audio only plays if you bend the wire at an awkward 45-degree angle.
[★1] Worst build quality imaginable - Rubber casing around the wire peeled off exposing bare copper strands within two weeks.
[★1] Shockingly bad longevity - Do not buy even if discounted to 200 rupees. It is disposable electronic waste.
[★1] Static shock and buzzing noise - Continuous buzzing ground loop hiss audible in background during music pauses.
[★1] Defective piece received - Right ear volume was 50% lower than left ear right out of the sealed retail box.
[★1] Earbuds fell apart - Glued plastic housing split open exposing the driver magnet while pulling it out of my bag.
[★1] Useless customer support - Warranty claim requires you to ship the broken earphone at your own courier expense which costs half the earphone price.
[★1] Avoid this product - Horrible durability, tinny audio, and zero reliability. Spend a few hundred rupees more on a reputable brand.
[★1] Complete disaster - Died within one week of purchase. Extremely frustrating purchase experience.
